intervals.label: reactor operation
intervals.locator: Portal on Nuclear Safety, Brokdorf page, "Operational data" table
intervals.note: Start is the first grid synchronisation (14 October 1986); first criticality was 8 October 1986 and commercial operation began 22 December 1986 (same table). End is the expiry of the authorisation for power operation under the Atomic Energy Act; BASE confirms the plant went off the grid for good on 31 December 2021.
intervals.quote: First grid synchronisation14 October 1986 ... Expiry of authorisation for power operation in accordance with the German Atomic Energy Act (AtG)31 December 2021

intervals.label: decommissioned
intervals.locator: BASE page "Abschaltung des Atomkraftwerks Brokdorf", introduction
intervals.note: The CONUS experiment's own setup at this site continued taking background(-only) data for some time after the reactor's own shutdown, before physically relocating to Leibstadt in 2023 (see experiment:conus); this interval describes the reactor/facility itself, not the CONUS detector's own operating window. The CONUS 2024 paper (arXiv:2401.07684) says the reactor 'stopped operation by the end of 2021'.
intervals.quote: Am 31.12.2021 ging das Atomkraftwerk Brokdorf endgültig vom Netz.

name: Brokdorf Nuclear Power Plant
notes: Original host facility of the CONUS experiment (CONUS data taking 2018-2022; the setup moved to Switzerland in 2023); operated as CONUS+ at facility:leibstadt-nuclear-power-plant from late 2023.

Reactor thermal power (3.9 GWth) is from arXiv:2011.00210 and agrees with the 3,900 MW thermal power on the Portal on Nuclear Safety data sheet (src:dw-nuklearesicherheit-brokdorf), which also gives the pressurised-water (pre-Convoy) type and 1,480 MW gross / 1,410 MW net electric capacity; these are stated in the technical summary and not as separate numeric specs.

summary.plain: A now-closed German nuclear power plant on the Elbe river that hosted the CONUS reactor-neutrino experiment from 2018 until the setup moved to Switzerland in 2023.
summary.technical: Brokdorf Nuclear Power Plant (KBR), Schleswig-Holstein, Germany; 3.9 GWth pressurised water reactor (1,480 MWe gross, 1,410 MWe net), first synchronised to the grid 1986-10-14 and shut down 2021-12-31 as part of Germany's nuclear phase-out; hosted the CONUS CEvNS experiment 17.1 m from the reactor core.
